# Buy a business

> A guide to buying a small business (entrepreneurship through acquisition, ETA, search funds, self-funded search, SBA 7(a) acquisitions), plus agent skills. Ten stages, about 245 question-shaped topics, answers with dated primary sources, practitioner clips, and one skill per topic. Human version: https://smallbizacqs.com. Install the skills: `npx skills add smallbizacqs/buy-a-business`.

Start with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/AGENTS.md. Nothing here is legal, tax or financial advice.

## Stages
- [1. Should you buy a business?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/01-decide.md): What buying a small business involves, what it costs you in time, money and risk, and whether you'd run it yourself.
- [2. Choose your path and line up the money](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/02-fund.md): Self-funded with an SBA loan, a search fund, a holding company or deal-by-deal investors, and how each is financed.
- [3. Decide what to buy and find deals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/03-find.md): Your criteria (the "buy box"), brokers and marketplaces, reaching owners directly, and how long a search takes.
- [4. Talk to owners and brokers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/04-approach.md): First calls and meetings, earning an owner's trust, working with brokers, and the early screen before an offer.
- [5. Size it up: real earnings, fair price, what you can borrow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/05-evaluate.md): Seller's discretionary earnings and add-backs, valuation multiples, debt coverage, and the risks that change the price.
- [6. Make the offer (the LOI)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/06-offer.md): The letter of intent, deal structure, working capital, negotiation, and the advisors you'll need.
- [7. Check everything and finalize the loan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/07-confirm.md): Financial, legal and operational due diligence, when to walk away, and the lender's approval process.
- [8. Sign and close](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/08-close.md): The purchase agreement and closing day. In small deals, signing and closing usually happen on the same day.
- [9. Your first 100 days as owner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/09-own.md): The seller's transition, keeping employees and customers, and what to change (and not change) first.
- [10. Later: grow, buy more, or sell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/guide/10-later.md): Growing value, add-on acquisitions and holding companies, and exit options.

## Skills
- [acquired-business-operating-system](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/acquired-business-operating-system/SKILL.md): Set up how an owner runs a small business they bought, once the first months are behind them: a weekly and monthly meeting rhythm, a scorecard of key numbers, how to hire and strengthen the team, where AI can help in operations, and whether to join a peer group or set up an advisory board.
- [acquisition-deal-model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/acquisition-deal-model/SKILL.md): Build an acquisition model for a small business purchase that works for the lender, the seller and the buyer: sources and uses, the capital stack (bank or SBA debt, seller note, buyer and investor equity), annual debt service by year, debt service coverage on EBITDA over combined debt service against the 1.25x SOP 50 10 8.1 screen, the largest bank loan the earnings support, owner pay after debt service, and EBITDA sensitivity.
- [acquisition-equity-sources](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/acquisition-equity-sources/SKILL.md): Map where the buyer's equity (down payment) for a small business purchase could come from: savings, a gift, a home equity line (HELOC), a 401(k) rollover structure (ROBS), a personal loan, family, investors, a seller note, and what each puts at risk, what it costs, and whether it counts toward an SBA equity injection under the sourced SOP 50 10 8.1 rules.
- [acquisition-go-no-go-review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/acquisition-go-no-go-review/SKILL.md): Run the go, reprice or walk-away review on a small-business acquisition: set walk-away criteria before diligence, sort diligence findings into deal-killers, reprice items, structure fixes and accepted risks, check results against the lines set in advance with a script (including debt service coverage at verified numbers), and write a dated decision memo in decisions.md.
- [acquisition-search-plan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/acquisition-search-plan/SKILL.md): Turn a buy box into a search plan: a realistic timeline, funnel math from the user's own conversion assumptions (contacts to conversations to CIMs to LOIs to a close), a weekly cadence, and a search budget with months of runway, with a tested script for the arithmetic.
- [add-on-acquisition-plan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/add-on-acquisition-plan/SKILL.md): Decide whether and when to buy a second business or an add-on, and plan it: readiness gates for the first business, the logic and risks of a roll-up (buy-and-build), what multiple arbitrage really depends on, an integration plan, and how to run several companies under a holding company.
- [ai-disruption-risk-check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/ai-disruption-risk-check/SKILL.md): Check, service by service, whether AI could replace what a specific small business sells, let competitors undercut it, or cut its costs, using evidence (customer behavior, pricing, competitor offerings, tests actually run) instead of hype in either direction.
- [am-i-ready-to-buy-a-business](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/am-i-ready-to-buy-a-business/SKILL.md): Run a readiness review for someone thinking about buying a small business: money and runway, appetite for a personal guarantee, operator skills and temperament, time and family, partner or solo, and the gaps to close first.
- [business-acquisition-criteria](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/business-acquisition-criteria/SKILL.md): Build or tighten a buyer's "buy box": the written criteria for which small businesses to look at (industry, size by SDE or EBITDA and price, geography, owner role, revenue quality, deal-breakers), saved as buy-box.yaml so every later skill screens against it.
- [business-broker-relations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/business-broker-relations/SKILL.md): Help a buyer look credible to business brokers and keep deals moving with them: a buyer profile and buy box one-pager, how to show proof of funds and financing, response-speed habits, a draft note to a broker about a listing, and what to do when a broker is slow or difficult.
- [business-owner-outreach](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/business-owner-outreach/SKILL.md): Prepare for and follow up on conversations with a business owner: the first call, the first meeting agenda, finding out why they're selling, what they care about besides price, and staying in touch with owners who aren't ready yet.
- [business-owner-take-home-pay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/business-owner-take-home-pay/SKILL.md): Work out what an owner actually takes home from a small business after loan payments, year by year: SDE, manager pay if any, a capital spending reserve, bank debt and seller note payments (including when a seller note comes off standby), an optional tax set-aside, and how long until pay reaches the buyer's target (the J-curve).
- [buy-a-business](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/buy-a-business/SKILL.md): Start here to buy a small business: sets up a workspace that carries over between sessions, finds out where the buyer is (just curious, searching, or mid-deal), asks one round of questions with a suggested answer for each, then names the stage, the guide page and the next one to three skills.
- [buy-vs-start-a-business](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/buy-vs-start-a-business/SKILL.md): Compare buying an existing small business, starting one from scratch, buying a franchise resale and opening a new franchise, against the buyer's own money, skills, timeline and appetite for risk, and write a one-page recommendation with the reasons and what would change it.
- [choose-acquisition-advisors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/choose-acquisition-advisors/SKILL.md): Put together the advisor team for buying a small business: deal lawyer, CPA, quality of earnings (QoE) provider, lender, and insurance broker, plus specialists when needed.
- [find-businesses-for-sale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/find-businesses-for-sale/SKILL.md): Search listed businesses for sale (broker listings and marketplaces such as BizBuySell, Acquire.com, TrustMRR and Flippa) against the user's buy box, record each match with its source and date, and add rows to pipeline.csv.
- [first-100-days-after-acquisition](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/first-100-days-after-acquisition/SKILL.md): Plan a new owner's first 100 days after buying a small business: listen before changing, protect cash and customers, set up weekly numbers and financial controls, decide when (and whether) to raise prices, and lead the team as the new owner.
- [grill-my-deal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/grill-my-deal/SKILL.md): Stress-test a small-business acquisition before you offer, sign or close: reads everything in the workspace, then asks every open question at once (price and earnings, financing and coverage, customers, owner dependence, employees, lease, licenses, working capital, your own capacity and downside), each with a recommended answer, and writes a record of decisions, accepted risks, deal-killers and open questions.
- [loi-for-small-business-acquisition](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/loi-for-small-business-acquisition/SKILL.md): Draft or review a letter of intent (LOI) to buy a small business: price, asset or stock structure, cash at close, seller note, earnout, working capital peg, exclusivity (no-shop), conditions, and which terms are binding.
- [off-market-deal-sourcing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/off-market-deal-sourcing/SKILL.md): Plan and draft direct outreach to owners of businesses that aren't listed for sale: build a target list from public and paid data, set up referral sources (CPAs, attorneys, bankers, wealth managers), and draft letters, cold emails and call scripts that the user sends.
- [owner-operator-vs-absentee-owner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/owner-operator-vs-absentee-owner/SKILL.md): Decide whether to run an acquired small business yourself or put in a general manager, with the math: what a manager costs, what that does to earnings, debt coverage and the owner's pay, and whether a target business is really ready to run without its owner.
- [personal-guarantee-risk-review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/personal-guarantee-risk-review/SKILL.md): Lay out what a personal guarantee and collateral on an acquisition loan (including an SBA 7(a) loan) put at risk: who signs, what is pledged, what could be owed if the business fails in year 1, 2, 3 or 5, and the questions to settle with a spouse, the lender and a lawyer before signing.
- [professionalize-small-business](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/professionalize-small-business/SKILL.md): Make a small business run without its owner and worth more: score how much it depends on the owner, write standard operating procedures (SOPs), hand off work in stages, put in the systems and reporting a future buyer or lender would expect, and build a value-creation plan with measures.
- [sba-7a-acquisition-loan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/sba-7a-acquisition-loan/SKILL.md): Explain how an SBA 7(a) loan to buy a business works and get the buyer lender-ready: the sourced SOP 50 10 8.1 basics (who lends, loan cap, 10-year amortization, equity injection and what counts, seller note on full standby, valuation and quality of earnings triggers, 1.25x coverage), the equity math on the buyer's numbers, a document checklist, and a side-by-side for comparing lenders.
- [sba-dscr-and-affordability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/sba-dscr-and-affordability/SKILL.md): Work out what a buyer can pay for a small business given the loan payments: debt service coverage (DSCR) at a target ratio, the highest price and senior loan the earnings support, and how the answer moves with the rate, the seller note, equity and a drop in earnings.
- [sba-lender-package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/sba-lender-package/SKILL.md): Run the lender side of a small-business acquisition: assemble the lender package (buyer documents, business financials, LOI and purchase agreement), track term sheets side by side, and build a timeline counted back from the target closing date so lender approval, third-party reports and closing conditions fit inside exclusivity.
- [sba-sop-rule-check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/sba-sop-rule-check/SKILL.md): Check a specific deal's structure against the SBA SOP 50 10 8.1 rules quoted in the repo's sources, with pinpoint citations: equity injection and what counts, seller note standby, price versus valuation, total debt cap, quality of earnings trigger, loan cap and amortization, debt service coverage (1.25x for an initial acquisition on EBITDA over combined debt service), earnouts, seller consulting period, lease term.
- [screen-business-cim](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/screen-business-cim/SKILL.md): Run the early screen on a business for sale: NDA basics to raise with a lawyer, reading a teaser or CIM (confidential information memorandum) for what it says and what it leaves out, early red flags that justify passing, and the short document request to send before making an offer.
- [sde-and-add-backs-analysis](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/sde-and-add-backs-analysis/SKILL.md): Rebuild a small business's real earnings from the tax returns and books: seller's discretionary earnings (SDE) and EBITDA, an add-back schedule with every item marked supported, assumed or unsupported, the cost of replacing the owner, and why the tax returns and P&L differ.
- [search-fund-investor-raise](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/search-fund-investor-raise/SKILL.md): Plan raising money from investors to search for or buy a small business (search capital, deal equity for one acquisition, or a holding company): what to raise and on what terms (preferred return, carry, ownership, governance), what investors look for, the materials to prepare, and a securities counsel gate before any outreach, with Rule 506(b) versus 506(c) explained at a high level from the cited federal rules.
- [search-fund-vs-sba-loan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/search-fund-vs-sba-loan/SKILL.md): Compare the main paths to buying a small business: a self-funded search with an SBA 7(a) loan, a traditional investor-backed search fund, an independent sponsor raising money deal by deal, and a holding company.
- [seller-note-structuring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/seller-note-structuring/SKILL.md): Design and compare seller note (seller financing) terms for a small business purchase: amount, rate, amortization, standby, interest accrual, balloon, security, subordination and set-off, with payment schedules from a tested script, the effect on the buyer's coverage and take-home, the SOP 50 10 8.1 rules that apply when an SBA loan sits alongside it, and a term sheet with talking points for the seller.
- [seller-transition-plan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/seller-transition-plan/SKILL.md): Plan the handover from the seller to the new owner: how long the seller stays and doing what, a week-by-week knowledge transfer, how and when to tell employees and customers, how to keep key people and accounts, and what to do when the seller won't let go.
- [small-business-acquisition-negotiation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-acquisition-negotiation/SKILL.md): Plan the negotiation to buy a small business from its owner: what the seller actually cares about, trading price against terms (cash at close, seller note, earnout, transition, timing), keeping a deal from stalling, and when changing the price after diligence (a retrade or reprice) is fair and how to raise it with evidence.
- [small-business-closing-checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-closing-checklist/SKILL.md): Build the closing-day checklist for buying a small business: who signs what, the funds flow (sources and uses that must balance to the dollar), a full list of closing costs, the questions to settle about the buying entity, and what must work on day one (bank account, payroll, insurance, licenses, keys and passwords).
- [small-business-deal-structure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-deal-structure/SKILL.md): Lay out the structure options for buying a small business and what each means for the buyer: asset vs stock purchase, cash at close vs seller note vs earnout, seller rollover equity, buying a majority now and the rest later, the seller's consulting or transition agreement, non-compete and non-solicit, and leasing vs buying the seller's real estate.
- [small-business-exit-options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-exit-options/SKILL.md): Lay out an owner's exit options for a small business and how to prepare: selling to a private equity firm, a strategic or industry buyer, a search fund or individual buyer, or employees; refinancing or recapitalizing to take money out; or keeping it.
- [small-business-financial-due-diligence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-financial-due-diligence/SKILL.md): Plan and run financial due diligence after a signed LOI on a small business: a financial request list, a diligence calendar counted back from the exclusivity end date, phased spending so the buyer doesn't pay for a full quality of earnings (QoE) report on a deal that dies in week two, QoE scoping, and a review guide for what comes back (tax returns vs P&L, bank deposits, AR aging, customer concentration, payroll, sales tax).
- [small-business-legal-due-diligence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-legal-due-diligence/SKILL.md): Organize legal due diligence on a small-business acquisition for the buyer and their lawyer: a legal request list (entity records, key contracts and whether they can be assigned, the lease and landlord consent, licenses and permits, litigation, liens and taxes, IP, domains and software, environmental, industry regulation), public-record searches the buyer can run, a contract and license inventory, and a "questions for counsel" memo.
- [small-business-operational-due-diligence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-operational-due-diligence/SKILL.md): Plan operational due diligence on a small business after the LOI: customer calls (with the seller's consent, a script and a notes template), employees, payroll and worker classification, key-person risk, systems and data quality, marketing and where new customers come from, insurance and loss runs, and a plan for shadowing the owner or working in the business before closing.
- [small-business-purchase-agreement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-purchase-agreement/SKILL.md): Walk a buyer through the purchase agreement for a small business (asset purchase agreement or stock purchase agreement): what each key term does, how it ties back to the LOI, and a written list of questions to take to counsel.
- [small-business-risk-assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-risk-assessment/SKILL.md): Build a risk register for a small business you're thinking of buying: customer and supplier concentration, owner dependence, key employees, licenses held by one person, labor, private equity roll-ups, interest rates and tariffs, turnaround risk and missed upside, each scored with the evidence behind it.
- [small-business-valuation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/small-business-valuation/SKILL.md): Estimate what a small business is worth as a price range under stated assumptions: how earnings multiples work, what moves a multiple up or down for this business, the gap between the asking price and the range, and how sensitive the price is to earnings.
- [verify-seller-financials](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/verify-seller-financials/SKILL.md): Run a proof of cash on a seller's numbers: tie monthly bank deposits to booked revenue and to the gross receipts on the tax returns, classify deposits that aren't sales (transfers, loans, owner money), and produce a numbered gap list for the seller to explain.
- [what-small-business-to-buy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/what-small-business-to-buy/SKILL.md): Turn a buyer's skills, money, location and risk tolerance into a scored shortlist of small business types to pursue, with the reasons, the cautions for a first-time buyer, and the questions that would move an industry up or down.
- [working-capital-peg-for-small-business](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallbizacqs/buy-a-business/main/skills/working-capital-peg-for-small-business/SKILL.md): Work out net working capital (NWC) for a small-business acquisition and propose a working-capital target (the peg) from trailing monthly balance sheets, with a tested script that computes the peg, flags seasonality and a pre-sale drawdown, and sizes the closing true-up.
